How Optimizing Nginx and Cloudflare Configuration Reduced Cloud Run Data Transfer Costs by 96%
item.description: The author of a personal blog hosted on Google Cloud Run discovered significant cost savings by reviewing and optimizing their nginx and Cloudflare configurations. Previously, their monthly Google Cloud bill had exceeded ¥1,000 for about a year, but after implementing two key changes, it dropped to ¥72 in October. The primary issue was that nginx gzip compression was disabled, causing Cloud Run to send uncompressed data to Cloudflare, which was then billed as data transfer. By enabling gzip compression, the size of the index.xml feed (which accounted for over 90% of data transfer) was reduced from 5.4 MB to 1.27 MB. Additionally, the author configured Cloudflare to cache HTML content and the index.xml feed, which reduced the number of requests to Cloud Run. Before the changes, Cloud Run data transfer costs were ¥556 in September, but after optimization, they dropped to ¥24 in October, representing a 96% reduction. item.title: Macquarie Island: The Only Place on Earth Where You Can Walk on the Mantle
item.description: Macquarie Island, located approximately 1,000 kilometers from the nearest landmass, is a unique geological site that allows visitors to walk directly on the Earth's mantle. This remote island, situated between Tasmania and Antarctica, is the only place on the planet where the mantle is exposed at the surface. The island's geological significance stems from its position on a 1,600-kilometer-long underwater fault line between the Australian and Pacific tectonic plates. Unlike most locations where mantle material is only accessible through volcanic activity or deep drilling, Macquarie Island provides direct access to the mantle due to its unique tectonic setting. The island has a rich history of human interaction, including early European exploration in the early 19th century, a period of intense hunting of seals and penguins for their oil, and later becoming a scientific research site. The article notes that this appearance could lead to more opportunities for Talarico in the entertainment industry, potentially expanding his reach beyond his current fan base.

item.title: Dale Evans: Iconic Western Star and Songwriter Remembered
item.description: Dale Evans (1912–2001) was an American actress, singer, and songwriter who earned the title 'Queen of the West' through her enduring career in film and television. Born Frances Octavia Smith in Texas, Evans began her professional journey in radio before transitioning to film in the 1940s. She became widely recognized for her partnership with singing cowboy Roy Rogers, both on-screen and in real life, as they starred together in over two dozen Western films and the long-running television series The Roy Rogers Show. Evans co-wrote the iconic song 'Happy Trails,' which became their signature theme and remains a beloved piece of Western entertainment history. Beyond her work in entertainment, Evans was a committed Christian author and speaker, sharing her faith through writing and public speaking engagements. item.title: Study links reproductive history and hormone therapy to brain vessel health in women
item.description: A recent study published in Neurology has uncovered a potential association between reproductive history, hormone therapy, and brain vascular health in women. The research, which examined 352 women with an average age of 70, found that longer reproductive lifespans correlated with fewer signs of damage to small brain blood vessels. Women who used oral contraceptives or menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) also showed some indicators of improved brain health, including stronger connections between brain regions and reduced vascular damage. The study's authors note that while these findings are intriguing, the research is observational and cannot establish causation. Alzheimer's Research UK, the UK's leading dementia research charity, has commented that the results are 'interesting' but emphasize the need for further research. item.description: The interview with Ken Light, a renowned photographer and educator, explores the evolving nature of documentary photography and the ethical responsibilities of photographers in the digital age. He emphasizes the importance of ethical practice, visual education, and the need for photographers to develop a critical eye that goes beyond mere observation. Light reflects on his own career, from photographing communities like Soul City to documenting workers in California, and how the industry has shifted from a predominantly white male perspective to one that values local, culturally informed perspectives. item.description: Recent cyberattacks targeting internet-connected refrigerators across multiple countries have highlighted significant security vulnerabilities in critical infrastructure systems. item.title: Surgical Resection Preferred Over SABR for Early-Stage NSCLC in Medically Suitable Patients, Study Finds
item.description: A large population-based study published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology has found that surgical resection remains the preferred curative-intent treatment for medically suitable patients with early-stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The research, conducted by Eva Kagenaar and colleagues from the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, analyzed data from 12,546 patients with T1–2N0M0 NSCLC diagnosed between 2015 and 2020 who received either stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) or surgical resection. After adjustment using instrumental variable methodology, the three-year all-cause mortality was 30.3% following SABR compared with 21.6% after surgery, representing an absolute risk difference of 8.8 percentage points (95% CI 1.4–16.2; p=0.02). Lung cancer-specific mortality also numerically favored surgery, though the difference did not reach statistical significance. item.title: Blindness and Musical Training Enhance Sound Processing Through Brain Plasticity
item.description: A recent study published in the Journal of Neuroscience reveals that individuals who have been blind since early childhood develop more consistent sound processing abilities compared to sighted individuals. The research examined nine participants who became blind before age two and 18 sighted individuals with varying musical training. Participants completed two hearing tasks: detecting tones against background noise and identifying pitch differences between two tones. The study found that blind participants performed better in pitch discrimination, suggesting their enhanced hearing stems from brain processing rather than ear sensitivity. Researchers discovered that blind individuals exhibited lower 'internal noise' in their auditory systems, meaning their brains processed sounds more reliably. item.title: NASA's Swift Observatory Completes 22-Year Mission with Atmospheric Re-Entry Over Indonesia
item.description: NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, a pioneering space telescope designed to study some of the universe's most violent cosmic events, has re-entered Earth's atmosphere over Indonesia after nearly 22 years in space. Launched in 2004 with a planned two-year mission, Swift far exceeded its expected lifespan, transforming our understanding of gamma-ray bursts, black holes, and supernovae. The spacecraft, equipped with three telescopes capable of detecting multiple wavelengths of light, was able to rapidly respond to sudden cosmic events, redirecting its instruments toward the source and alerting observatories worldwide. This capability allowed scientists to study brief astronomical phenomena before they faded from view. Swift's observations contributed to groundbreaking research on active galaxies powered by supermassive black holes, X-ray flares from stars, and supernovae. item.title: Rock Creek Lake: A Hidden Alpine Gem in the Sierra Nevada Offering Camping, Fishing, and Hiking Trails
item.description: Rock Creek Lake, situated within Inyo National Forest at approximately 9,600 feet in elevation, presents a compelling alternative to the overcrowded alpine destinations of Big Bear and Lake Tahoe. Unlike Big Bear, which is a manmade reservoir, Rock Creek Lake is a true alpine lake, offering visitors a pristine high-altitude experience. The lake, covering 55 surface acres, provides exceptional trout fishing opportunities in both the lake and Rock Creek, with species including brook, brown, cutthroat, rainbow, and California's state fish, the golden trout. Anglers can access the lake via a concrete boat ramp open from late April until snowfall, with a 5 mph speed limit on the lake. Shore access is available around the lake and along portions of the creek for bank fishing and wading. The fishing season runs from the last Saturday in April until November 15, requiring a valid California fishing license for those 16 and older. item.description: EA has announced the remastered releases of 25 classic games from the 1990s, including several Wing Commander titles and nearly the entire Ultima series, now available on Steam and GOG. The remasters feature enhanced full-motion video sequences, 60 frames-per-second gameplay, and improved controller support, though some users report issues with controller functionality. The project began when EA senior producer Jim Vessella discovered a physical media archive at EA's Redwood Shores campus containing original masters of Wing Commander III and IV. With the help of community members like Matt Wells, who developed community patches for Wing Commander games, the team digitized and restored the footage, working 17 hours a day on swing shifts. For Privateer 2, the team contacted the original cinematics director, Steve Hilliker, who had the tapes in his attic and provided new color grading. item.title: Israel's President Assigns Opposition Leader to Form Coalition Amid Political Uncertainty
item.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has tasked opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new government following the October 27 elections, marking a significant step toward potentially ousting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving premier. Eisenkot, a former military chief and leader of the Yashar party, has six weeks to assemble a coalition in a deeply divided nation still reeling from the October 7, 2023, Hamas attacks and subsequent conflicts in Gaza. The political landscape remains complex as no single bloc secured a parliamentary majority, leaving Arab-led parties as potential kingmakers—a role they have held only once in Israel's history. Netanyahu's Likud party, the largest in parliament, lost its majority, while Eisenkot's coalition also fell short. item.title: Trump Faces Mockery After Saying He Could Stop Insulting Democrats to Reach Political Deals
item.description:
President Donald Trump faced criticism and ridicule after claiming he could easily go six months without insulting Democrats if doing so helped secure political agreements. The exchange took place during an interview with CBS correspondent Ross Douthat for the television program 60 Minutes, scheduled to air Sunday.
Douthat raised the question after Trump discussed Senator-elect James Talarico, who had reportedly expressed interest in working with the president on immigration policy during an appearance on Fox News. The interviewer reminded Trump that he had previously mocked Talarico during the campaign, using the nickname “TalaFREAKo.” Trump acknowledged making the remark but insisted he could cooperate with Democrats without repeatedly insulting them.
However, when Douthat asked whether he could refrain from such comments for six months, Trump answered that he could do so very easily. He then undermined that assurance by adding that he also refers to many Democrats as “dumbocrats.”

item.title: AlpineBSD: A New AI-Free BSD-Based Operating System Combining NetBSD and Alpine Linux
item.description: AlpineBSD has been announced as a new operating system in the BSD family, aiming to provide a FOSS (Free and Open Source Software) solution that avoids the use of AI-generated code. The project combines NetBSD's kernel and libc with a port of the Alpine Linux userland, positioning itself as a clean, minimalistic alternative to mainstream Linux distributions. While still in its early stages with no installation media available, AlpineBSD has already established an AI policy stating that any software containing output from generative AI tools, such as LLMs, is considered 'tainted' for the project. This aligns with NetBSD's 2024 guidelines, which also prohibit AI-generated code in their commit process. The project's source code and ports repository are hosted on Sourcehut under the account of sircmpwn (Drew DeVault), a well-known figure in the open-source community. item.title: Geological Study Links Mantle Convection to Great Unconformity Formation
item.description: The Great Unconformity, a significant gap in the geological record where Cambrian sedimentary rocks rest atop much older crystalline rocks, has puzzled geologists for decades. Recent research published in Nature by Nicolas Flament and Santosh Dhungana proposes that Earth's mantle dynamics played a crucial role in creating this geological feature. Their models suggest that slow mantle convection currents pushed continents upward for hundreds of millions of years, allowing glaciers to erode the surface before the land sank again, creating the distinctive unconformity. The study explains why this feature is most prominent in North America and parts of northern Europe and China, while other regions show different patterns. The researchers found that Laurentia, the ancient core of North America, experienced prolonged uplift followed by subsidence during the Cambrian period, which combined with the Snowball Earth glaciation to create the ideal conditions for the Great Unconformity. item.description: A comprehensive study spanning up to 43 years has revealed that consuming two to three cups of caffeinated coffee daily is associated with a significantly lower risk of dementia and improved cognitive functioning. item.title: November Sky Offers Meteor Showers, Planetary Pairing, and Voyager 1 Milestone
item.description: November 2026 presents a remarkable celestial display with multiple astronomical events. The Southern Taurid meteor shower peaks around November 5, followed by the Northern Taurids on November 12, both offering occasional bright fireballs. Mars and Jupiter will appear unusually close together on November 15-16, separated by just 1.2 degrees in the southeastern sky before sunrise. The Leonid meteor shower provides additional viewing opportunities on November 17-18. NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft reaches a historic milestone on November 17, becoming the first human-made object to travel one light-day from Earth, meaning radio signals take 24 hours to reach it. A full supermoon on November 24 begins a sequence of three consecutive supermoons, with the Moon appearing slightly larger and brighter when it coincides with its closest orbital approach to Earth. item.description: The Spanish Civil War (1936-1939) was marked by intense internal conflicts within both the Republican and Nationalist factions. item.title: LangGraph SQL Agent Optimizes Database Queries by Limiting Schema Exposure
item.description: The article discusses a new LangGraph SQL agent developed by Ashish Sinha that addresses a common inefficiency in text-to-SQL agents. Most existing agents include the entire database schema in every prompt, which becomes costly and inefficient for large databases where only a small portion of tables is relevant to the query. The new agent, implemented in the schemagate library, uses a four-node LangGraph workflow to optimize this process. The first node, select_schema, uses a SchemagateRetriever to identify only the necessary tables for a given question, operating offline without requiring a model call. The second node, write_sql, generates a SELECT statement using only those selected tables. The third node, run_sql, executes the query and handles errors by sending feedback to the model if the query fails. This chiral signature, which indicates handedness in the material's magnetic structure, is a key characteristic of altermagnetism that distinguishes it from conventional antiferromagnets. The study, published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, analyzed a 115-million-year-old theropod dinosaur bone from Brazil's Romualdo Formation. The fossil, a partial hind limb of Aratasaurus museunacionali, contained microscopic structures resembling red blood cells within vascular canals, along with chemical evidence of heme—a molecule found in hemoglobin. This is the first time heme has been detected in situ within fossilized structures. The research team used advanced imaging and chemical analysis to confirm the presence of these structures, suggesting that low-oxygen burial conditions at the site may have preserved organic material. item.title: A neural network that mimics an if statement using arithmetic operations
item.description: This article explores the creation of a neural network that replicates the behavior of a simple if statement in programming. The goal is to produce the same output as a conditional statement that returns 10 when a variable 'a' is greater than 4 and 12 otherwise. The approach involves constructing a fixed list of arithmetic operations rather than training the network. The process begins by defining a 'flag' variable that acts as a decision maker, using two ReLU (rectified linear unit) functions to determine whether 'a' is greater than 4. item.description:

These shrines, some dating back over three hundred years, were constructed by local households rather than the Church as a way for families to display their patron saints or the Virgin Mary publicly while seeking protection for their homes. The architectural styles vary widely: some feature elaborate stone niches with carved saints beneath Baroque canopies, while others are simpler painted figures behind glass, often accompanied by plastic flowers and small lamps that are still lit at night. These shrines form an open-air gallery of Maltese folk devotion that most tourists overlook as they head toward the Citadel, a major historical site in Victoria.

item.description:
Former campaign staffers for Michigan Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens have described efforts to limit the influence of her fiancé, Jason Turkish, during her unsuccessful Senate primary campaign. According to more than a dozen former aides and people familiar with the campaign, senior staff members held a meeting without Stevens to discuss concerns about Turkish's growing involvement in campaign decisions.
Turkish, a disability lawyer and major campaign donor, had become one of Stevens' closest advisers and was secretly engaged to her by early June. item.title: Study Links Geometry and Color in Near-Death Experiences
item.description: A recent study published in Frontiers in Psychology has uncovered intriguing patterns in the spatial and visual elements of near-death experiences (NDEs). Researchers led by France Lerner from the University of Haifa asked 50 individuals who reported NDEs to draw maps of the spaces they recalled experiencing during these events. The participants' reconstructions revealed four main geometric categories: conical spaces (including the familiar tunnel), broad curved spaces, flatter curving spaces, and enveloping spherical or oval spaces. Notably, the study found a strong correlation between the geometry of these spaces and the colors associated with them. Conical spaces, such as tunnels, were predominantly perceived in black, white, gray, or achromatic tones (22 out of 28), while broad curved spaces were mostly experienced in color (27 out of 31). item.title: Austrian Painter Alois Arnegger Captures Alpine and Mediterranean Landscapes in Luminous Works
item.description: Alois Arnegger (1879–1963) was an Austrian landscape painter renowned for his vivid portrayals of the Alps and Mediterranean coastlines. Born in Vienna, he studied at the Academy of Fine Arts under Robert Russ and August Eisenmenger. His early works depicted the snow-capped mountains and rural landscapes of Austria, characterized by soft alpine light. After traveling to Italy in the 1920s, Arnegger shifted his focus to the sun-drenched shores of Naples, Capri, Sanremo, and other coastal areas, creating paintings marked by dramatic lighting, rich color palettes, and a romantic atmosphere. His ability to convey both the serene grandeur of mountainous terrain and the radiant warmth of Mediterranean settings became his signature. Arnegger's body of work includes numerous pieces such as 'A Forest Pond in the Evening Light,' 'A Northern Italian Lake,' 'A Scene in Sorrento,' and 'Alpine Glow over the Rosengarten,' among others. In Ireland, SuperValu, the country's third-largest supermarket chain, reported that 13 of its 223 stores were affected by a cyber incident involving a specific refrigerator model, resulting in the removal of chilled and frozen products from sale. Swedish stores operated by ICA and Co-op experienced similar issues, with freezer temperatures reaching 50°C overnight. Belgian and Luxembourgish stores under Ahold Delhaize also faced disruptions, with Carrefour reporting 15 out of 700 stores in Belgium affected and five Spar stores under Colruyt Group impacted. item.title: Russia Expands Its Influence in Africa but Remains Far Behind China Economically
item.description:
Russia has increased its influence across Africa over the past decade, but its economic presence remains significantly smaller than China's, according to an analysis published by bne IntelliNews on November 2, 2026. Based on the University of Denver's Foreign Bilateral Influence Capacity index, Russia's share of foreign influence in Africa rose from 2.2% in 2015 to 2.8% in 2024, moving it from 12th to ninth place among the continent's international partners. China leads with 11%, followed by France and the United States at 7% each.
Russia's growing influence is largely based on military cooperation, food exports, and nuclear energy projects rather than trade and investment. Bilateral trade with African countries reached $30.4 billion in 2025, more than double the 2015 figure. However, this represents only around 1.5% of Africa's foreign trade. China's merchandise trade with the continent reached a record $348 billion in 2025, more than 12 times Russia's total.

item.description: A Learjet traveling from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas crashed on Sunday afternoon near Palm Beach, Florida, resulting in nine fatalities. The aircraft, a Bombardier-made two-engine jet, encountered a thunderstorm cell at 35,000 feet around 12:48 p.m., with the co-pilot reporting light, clear ice and moderate turbulence to air traffic control. Federal officials have stated that ice and weather conditions were 'certainly a factor' in the crash, though the investigation is ongoing and may take months to conclude. item.title: White Dwarf's Debris Rings Offer Clues to Solar System's Future
item.description: Astronomers at the European Southern Observatory (ESO) have identified a white dwarf star, J1328−1450, located approximately 1,600 light-years from Earth, surrounded by two distinct rings of gas and dust. These debris rings, observed using the Very Large Telescope, are believed to be remnants of a planetary system that once orbited the star. As the star evolved from a red giant phase into a white dwarf, it likely destroyed some of its planets, leaving behind rocky bodies exposed to extreme conditions. The resulting debris formed the observed rings, which may provide insight into the future of our own solar system. In about 5 billion years, the Sun will exhaust its fuel, expand into a red giant, and potentially engulf nearby planets before shedding its outer layers to become a white dwarf. Any surviving rocky bodies could then break apart, forming a debris disk similar to the one observed around J1328−1450. In Ruston, Washington, children played in yards while a nearby smelter released toxic residue, and in Birmingham, Alabama, homes stood adjacent to a U.S. Steel plant, with industrial smog enveloping the area. item.description:

item.title: Supreme Court Rejects Trump's Request to Set Aside 20,000 California Ballots
item.description:
The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday rejected the Trump administration's emergency request to intervene in a Justice Department lawsuit seeking to set aside 20,000 ballots in California that officials flagged as potentially cast by noncitizens.
The Justice Department had argued that the ballots should be withheld until the citizenship of the voters could be verified. However, multiple lower courts had already rejected efforts to remove the ballots from the electoral process, finding insufficient grounds to justify such action. During court arguments, the DOJ also acknowledged that its list of potentially ineligible voters could contain significant errors.
The Supreme Court's decision prompted an angry reaction from several prominent supporters of President Donald Trump and conservative commentators on social media platform X. item.title: Walking Speed Linked to Lower Mortality Risk in Long-Term Study
item.description: A study published in JAMA Network Open followed 4,067 U.K. adults with an average age of 69 over nearly 12 years to examine the relationship between walking speed and mortality risk. Participants completed a walking test at their normal pace and wore wrist activity trackers for nine days to measure everyday walking speed. item.title: How Radiation Creates the Blue Color in Topaz Birthstones
item.description: The article explains that November's birthstone, topaz, often appears in a brilliant blue color in jewelry stores, but this blue is not natural. Instead, the stone is treated with radiation to alter its crystal structure, creating color centers that absorb specific wavelengths of light. The process involves ionizing radiation, which knocks electrons out of their normal states, leaving electron vacancies or 'holes.' These trapped electrons and holes form color centers that change the stone's appearance. The article clarifies that while radiation is used in the treatment, the resulting blue topaz is not radioactive. Neutron irradiation in a nuclear reactor can temporarily make the stone radioactive, but it is held until radioactivity decays to safe levels before sale. The mineral topaz, with the chemical formula Al₂SiO₄(F,OH)₂, contains fluorine but is not dangerous like hydrofluoric acid. item.title: Bfloat16 Rounding Issues Cause Near-Complete Stagnation in RL Policy Updates
item.description: The article discusses a critical issue in reinforcement learning (RL) post-training for language models, where standard bfloat16 (bf16) rounding discards over 99% of parameter updates. Modern frameworks like Verl, TRL, and OpenRLHF maintain master weights in fp32 within PyTorch but serve rollouts using a bf16 copy in inference engines such as vLLM or SGLang. The conversion from fp32 to bf16 uses round-to-nearest, which creates a 'dead zone' where small updates are rounded to zero. At typical RL learning rates (1e-6 to 3e-7), nearly all per-parameter updates fall below the threshold, causing the inference engine to serve a model that is effectively frozen. The Stanford paper by Andrew Gao and William Gao demonstrates that only 0.4-0.5% of weights change per optimizer step, with weights needing 50-200 steps to cross a bf16 grid boundary. This discrepancy leads to a significant mismatch between the trained model and the one used for rollouts, as evidenced by lower scores on checkpoints co

item.title: Human Activity Prevents Onset of Next Ice Age, Study Finds
item.description: A new study published in the journal Science suggests that human-driven climate change has halted the onset of the next ice age. Researchers led by Nicolás Young of Columbia University analyzed the Barnes Ice Cap (BIC) in Canada, which is a remnant of the Laurentide Ice Sheet (LIS) that once covered much of North America. The study used two primary methods: measuring cosmogenic beryllium-10 in rocks and analyzing carbon-14 in vegetation to track the ice cap's historical growth and retreat. The findings indicate that the next ice age was poised to begin around 2,000 years ago, as the Earth entered a cooling phase following the Holocene interglacial period. However, the expansion of the ice sheet was interrupted by rising global temperatures, particularly since the 1960s, when anthropogenic warming reversed the ice cap's growth. item.description: Luise 'Niddy' Impekoven (November 2, 1904 – November 20, 2002) was a German dancer who rose to international fame during the 1920s and 1930s as a leading figure in the modern German dance movement known as Ausdruckstanz. Starting as a child prodigy in the Weimar era, she transitioned into a celebrated expressionist dance superstar before retiring abruptly in 1934 at the age of 30. Impekoven's performances were characterized by dramatic, whimsical, and emotive styles, often set to classical music such as Beethoven's 'Moonlight Sonata.' She became particularly famous for her 'doll dances,' which mimicked jerky, puppet-like movements inspired by avant-garde artistic dolls. Her work resonated with elite intellectual circles, attracting admirers like authors Thomas Mann and Arthur Schnitzler. item.description: Gregory Kurtzer, the creator of Rocky Linux and former CentOS developer, has developed a new operating system kernel called Ginux in just 11 days with the assistance of AI. Unlike traditional Linux distributions, Ginux is not a fork of the Linux kernel but a completely independent, Rust-first x86-64 kernel. It features its own memory management, scheduler, process model, filesystems, networking, and device support, all written from scratch. The key innovation is that Ginux implements the Linux ABI (Application Binary Interface), allowing existing Linux binaries to run unmodified on the new system. This means users can run standard Linux applications without needing to recompile them, making it a direct compatibility layer rather than a replacement kernel. item.title: Byoky: Open-source wallet for AI API keys
item.description: Byoky is an open-source wallet designed to securely manage AI API keys, available as a Chrome and Firefox extension and as mobile apps for iOS and Android. The wallet allows users to store their API keys for various providers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Gemini, encrypted directly on their devices. item.description: The article details a technical quirk in the curl command-line tool that made it accidentally Turing-complete for a period of nine months, from version 8.12 through 8.16. This combination enabled curl to simulate any two-counter Minsky program, which is theoretically Turing-complete under idealized conditions of unbounded resources. The article explains the technical implementation, including how counter values were represented using string manipulations and how configuration files acted as labels for program states. A proof-of-concept demonstrating the addition of 2 + 3 was provided, along with instructions for building a local curl 8.12.0 binary to test the behavior. item.title: NASA Swift Observatory to Reenter Earth's Atmosphere Following Failed Rescue Attempt
item.description: The Swift Observatory, a NASA telescope launched in 2004 to study gamma-ray bursts and other cosmic phenomena, is on the verge of reentering Earth's atmosphere after a failed rescue mission. The U.S. Space Force predicts the 1.5-ton telescope will crash on or around Friday, with most of it burning up during reentry. However, some denser components made of tungsten and mirror parts may survive and potentially land in oceanic areas or over regions including Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, Central and South America. The telescope, which has operated for 22 years, was designed to rapidly respond to cosmic events, earning its name from its swift maneuverability. Its mission included discovering over 2,000 gamma-ray bursts and 1,400 supernovae, as well as observing comets, asteroids, and black holes. item.title: New research challenges comet theory as source of life's building blocks on Earth
item.description: A new study published in Scientific Reports challenges a decades-old theory that comets delivered the organic molecules necessary for life to Earth. The research, led by Richard Anslow of the University of Cambridge, used computer simulations to analyze comet impacts during Earth's early history. The findings suggest that the high-speed impacts would have destroyed fragile organic molecules rather than delivering them intact. The study simulated 100,000 comet impacts over 4 billion years ago, finding that 54% of simulations showed no impact at all, while only a 'tiny minority' of impacts (46%) had one to three collisions. Crucially, even successful impacts would have needed to occur in a 'perfect location' with existing conditions like liquid water and other chemicals, making the process unlikely. item.description: El microrrelato titulado 'Quizá hoy', escrito por Miscelánea, ha sido declarado ganador de la semana en el certamen de microrrelatos organizado por Deltha. La historia narra la espera de un personaje que, tras un periodo de silencio, escucha por fin una llamada que incluye su nombre. La narración se centra en la tensión creada por la espera y la esperanza de ser reconocido, culminando con una revelación irónica: la voz que llama no se dirige a la protagonista, sino que ordena a un dispositivo humanoide desconectar a Alexa. El texto, publicado el 8 de noviembre de 2026, refleja una narrativa breve pero cargada de significado, donde la espera y la ilusión se enfrentan a la realidad tecnológica. El microrrelato, al igual que otros trabajos presentados en Deltha, forma parte de una serie de historias cortas que se publican cada lunes, ofreciendo a los lectores una reflexión sobre la conexión humana en un mundo cada vez más automatizado. La trama, aunque breve, logra transmitir una profunda

item.title: Dana White rechaza propuesta de Trump para ser secretario de prensa de la Casa Blanca
item.description: El presidente Donald Trump anunció en su plataforma Truth Social que había ofrecido el puesto de secretario de prensa de Estados Unidos al CEO de UFC, Dana White, quien, según fuentes, declinó la propuesta. Trump publicó en su cuenta que White, a quien describió como 'un luchador y guerrero violento', había sido nombrado para el cargo, y solicitó que trajera seis luchadores de UFC para 'defenderse contra la Izquierda Loca'. Aunque un asistente del presidente sugirió que la propuesta era una broma, Trump ha estado buscando a alguien para reemplazar a Karoline Leavitt, quien dejó el puesto en agosto, y a Katie Zacharia, cuyo breve mandato duró solo cinco días. White, quien se ha convertido en uno de los aliados más visibles de Trump en los últimos años, se negó a comentar sobre la oferta durante una conferencia de prensa, aunque confirmó que planea reunirse con Trump en Washington el lunes. Trump ha tenido dificultades para llenar el puesto, especialmente después de que los demócratas ga

item.title: Alumnos de la Academia General del Aire de San Javier llevan tres meses sin recibir sus pagos
item.description: La asociación profesional Militares Con Futuro ha denunciado que los alumnos de la Academia General del Aire de San Javier, junto con los de la Academia General Militar de Zaragoza y la Academia General Básica de Suboficiales de Talarn, llevan tres meses sin percibir las retribuciones correspondientes a su formación militar. Según la asociación, estos futuros oficiales y suboficiales han tenido que depender económicamente de sus familias para cubrir sus gastos diarios mientras completan sus estudios. Militares Con Futuro ha presentado al Ministerio de Defensa 22 preguntas para aclarar el número de alumnos afectados, el importe adeudado y las causas del retraso en los pagos. La organización exige que las cantidades pendientes se abonen en la nómina de noviembre, junto con los intereses correspondientes, y que se determinen responsabilidades administrativas. Además, solicita información sobre si existe una investigación abierta y si el problema afecta a otros centros de formación militar

item.title: Macquarie: la única isla del mundo donde se puede caminar sobre el manto terrestre
item.description: La isla Macquarie, ubicada a más de 1.000 kilómetros de la masa terrestre más cercana (la Isla Sur de Nueva Zelanda), es el único lugar del planeta donde es posible caminar directamente sobre el manto terrestre. Geológicamente excepcional, la isla se encuentra en el límite entre las placas tectónicas australiana y del Pacífico, en una falla submarina de 1.600 kilómetros de largo. A diferencia de otros lugares donde el manto se expone parcialmente a través de actividad volcánica, en Macquarie el manto terrestre emerge en la superficie debido a la interacción de las placas tectónicas, permitiendo el acceso directo a esta capa planetaria que ocupa el 85% del volumen terrestre. La isla, que emergió hace entre 80.000 y 300.000 años, es extremadamente joven geológicamente y no ha estado habitada de manera permanente. Desde principios del siglo XX, Macquarie es considerada un santuario ecológico, incluida en el listado de Patrimonio de la Humanidad en los años 90. La única presencia humana co

item.title: Gemini como asistente de compras: consejos para encontrar, comparar y decidir sobre productos
item.description: La noticia explora cómo Google Gemini, la inteligencia artificial de Google, puede ser utilizada como asistente para la compra de productos. El artículo detalla varias estrategias para aprovechar al máximo esta herramienta, como definir claramente las necesidades y presupuesto, solicitar tablas comparativas con características específicas, utilizar la función de investigación profunda para compras costosas, buscar reseñas y opiniones en línea, y aprovechar la cámara del móvil para identificar productos en tiempo real. Se enfoca en cómo Gemini puede ayudar a los usuarios a encontrar, analizar y comparar productos antes de realizar una compra, ofreciendo ejemplos prácticos de prompts que pueden utilizarse para obtener resultados más precisos. El artículo también destaca la importancia de especificar requisitos como disponibilidad en el país, características técnicas, garantías y opiniones de otros usuarios para tomar decisiones informadas. Además, se menciona cómo Gemini puede ser útil p

item.title: Yemen ejecuta seis operaciones militares contra objetivos saudíes en respuesta a ataques civiles
item.description: Las Fuerzas Armadas de Yemen han anunciado la realización de seis operaciones militares utilizando misiles balísticos, de crucero y drones contra objetivos saudíes, en respuesta a los ataques recientes de Arabia Saudí que afectaron a zonas civiles en los distritos de Al-Waziyah y Bani Hushaysh, causando decenas de muertos y heridos, principalmente mujeres y niños, además de destruir viviendas. La primera operación se dirigió al Aeropuerto Internacional Rey Jalid, depósitos de petróleo y torre de destilación de Aramco en Riad. La segunda atacó las instalaciones de Aramco en Jurais, mientras que la tercera se enfocó en la estación de bombeo número 8 en Al-Dawadmi. La cuarta operación impactó en concentraciones de fuerzas saudíes en el campamento de la Guardia Nacional de Nayran, causando numerosas bajas. La quinta y sexta operaciones se llevaron a cabo en el este de la provincia de Al-Yauf y en los distritos de Ragwan y Madqal, respectivamente, bajo el mando del oficial saudí Faris al-Sh

item.title: Dos agricultores fallecen tras practicar ritual tradicional para resolver conflicto de tierras en Filipinas
item.description: En Filipinas, dos agricultores de la comunidad indígena Tagakaulo, Tonny Bulanon Mansag de 69 años y Gaspar Tusan Palasanon de 49 años, perdieron la vida tras participar en un ritual tradicional conocido como Sulif para resolver una disputa por un terreno. El ritual, que consiste en sumergirse bajo el agua y aguantar el mayor tiempo posible sin respirar, se llevó a cabo el 16 de octubre en el río Glamang de la localidad de Alabel, provincia de Sarangani, ante varios espectadores. Los hombres, sostenidos por otros dos con palos contra el agua, permanecieron sumergidos durante aproximadamente 12 minutos antes de ser retirados inconscientes. Mansag falleció al llegar al Hospital Provincial de Sarangani, mientras que Palasanon murió horas después en el centro médico. El presidente del Consejo Tribal Provincial de Sarangani, Datu Fulung Edmund D. Pangilan, emitió un comunicado advirtiendo sobre el mal uso de esta práctica tradicional sagrada. Explicó que el Sulif es una ceremonia ancestral

item.title: Ayuso critica a colectivos por ejercer derecho a huelga, vincula protestas con violencia y delincuencia
item.description: La presidenta de la Comunidad de Madrid, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, ha realizado una serie de críticas contra diversos colectivos que ejercen su derecho a la huelga y manifestarse, incluyendo a profesores, sanitarios, bomberos y personas que protestan por la vivienda. En una serie de declaraciones, Ayuso ha calificado a los profesores como "violentos" y "antidemocráticos", vinculando sus protestas con vandalismo y violencia, a pesar de que el derecho a la huelga está protegido por la Constitución Española. La presidenta también ha acusado a los sindicatos de ser una "mafia sindical" que secuestra las calles y busca incendiar las calles durante la campaña electoral. En el ámbito educativo, Ayuso ha criticado a los profesores que se manifiestan, calificándolos de "violentos" que buscan "reventar Madrid", y ha atribuido sus demandas a una "corrupción mafiosa". En el sector sanitario, ha criticado a los médicos por no negociar y ha calificado sus protestas como "políticas". En el caso de los bombe

item.title: acerca de la situación del intelectual latinoamericano
item.description: El texto analiza una controversia literaria en torno a una novela de la escritora peruana Silva Rojas, cuyo libro ha sido cuestionado por su posible uso de inteligencia artificial en su creación. El autor del ensayo, un escritor latinoamericano, reflexiona sobre cómo la industria editorial y los académicos están creando nuevos clichés al exigir que los escritores de tercer mundo escriban sobre temas como migración, agua, territorio y violencia contra las mujeres, en lugar de permitirles explorar otras temáticas. El ensayo critica la 'racismo benevolente' de la élite cultural latinoamericana que espera que los escritores de países en desarrollo se limiten a narrar su 'misery' y victimización. El autor también aborda el debate sobre el uso de IA en la literatura, expresando preocupación por cómo la tecnología está transformando la creación artística y cómo los intelectuales no están respondiendo adecuadamente a este cambio. El texto concluye con una reflexión sobre lo que debería ser una

item.title: Análisis de los vínculos históricos entre Donald Trump y Rusia desde la Guerra Fría hasta su presidencia
item.description: La noticia explora los vínculos históricos entre Donald Trump y Rusia, abarcando desde los años ochenta hasta su presidencia. El documental 'La sombra roja sobre la Casa Blanca' reconstruye una historia de espionaje, intereses económicos y maniobras políticas que se remontan a la Guerra Fría. Según testimonios de antiguos espías y responsables de inteligencia, los servicios secretos soviéticos buscaron establecer contactos con Trump en los años ochenta, cuando era un promotor inmobiliario de Nueva York. En 1987, las autoridades soviéticas le ofrecieron explorar la construcción de un hotel en Moscú, lo que representa un primer acercamiento. Oleg Kalugin, antiguo general de la KGB, reconoce que conocían información sobre Trump pero niega que estuviera controlado por la KGB. Decenas de años después, durante la campaña presidencial de 2016, Trump intentó en secreto construir una Torre Trump en Moscú a través de Felix Sater, mientras los servicios de inteligencia estadounidenses investigaba

item.title: El Gobierno de Navarra retira el acuerdo sobre impuesto a renovables tras publicación en prensa
item.description: El Gobierno de Navarra, liderado por el PSOE, ha decidido retirar un acuerdo que preveía la creación de un impuesto a las energías renovables, específicamente a los parques eólicos y fotovoltaicos, tras la publicación de la información por parte de El Periódico de la Energía. El consejero de Economía, José Luis Arasti, explicó que la publicación de la información derivó de una redacción errónea en un punto del acuerdo presupuestario, y tras conversaciones con EH Bildu-Nafarroa, se optó por retirar dicho punto para evitar interpretaciones equivocadas. Arasti destacó que Navarra ha sido, es y será líder en producción y autoconsumo de energía renovable, y que no se promoverá ningún impuesto al sol ni al viento. El Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y la asociación UNEF también se pronunciaron en apoyo de la decisión, celebrando que se haya retirado el impuesto y esperando que otras comunidades autónomas, como Castilla y León, sigan el mismo camino. La ministra Sara Aagesen, vicepresi

item.title: Negociación de servicios mínimos para la huelga general del 11 de noviembre en Madrid y otros sectores
item.description: La Comunidad de Madrid, Correos y el Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica están negociando los porcentajes de plantilla que deberán trabajar durante la huelga general del 11 de noviembre. Los sindicatos CCOO, UGT y CNT acusan a la Comunidad de Madrid de querer imponer servicios mínimos desproporcionados sin una negociación real. Los servicios mínimos son la parte de la plantilla obligada a trabajar durante una huelga para cubrir lo imprescindible, y según el artículo 10.2 del Real Decreto-ley 17/1977, son fijados por la autoridad gubernativa, no por las empresas. En Correos, por ejemplo, se propuso un 50% en unidades de distribución, un 25% en centros de tratamiento y un 100% en servicios rurales, lo que los sindicatos consideran 'abiertamente abusivos'. La doctrina constitucional exige que los servicios mínimos estén justificados y sean la mínima cobertura necesaria, no un porcentaje excesivo que vacíe la huelga. En el pasado, casos como los mínimos del 100% en residencias gallegas

item.title: La consultora Equilibra estima que la pobreza en Argentina alcanza el 45,4%, superando en 13,1 puntos al INDEC
item.description: La consultora económica Equilibra ha presentado una nueva medición que estima que el 45,4% de la población argentina vive bajo la línea de pobreza durante el primer semestre de 2026, lo que representa aproximadamente 21,1 millones de personas. Este cálculo contrasta significativamente con el dato oficial del Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos (INDEC), que informa una tasa del 32,3% para el mismo período. La diferencia entre ambas estimaciones asciende a 13,1 puntos porcentuales, equivalente a unos seis millones de personas adicionales en situación de pobreza según la metodología de Equilibra. La principal divergencia radica en la composición de la canasta básica utilizada para determinar la línea de pobreza. Mientras el INDEC se basa en patrones históricos, Equilibra actualiza la metodología mediante la Encuesta Nacional de Gastos de los Hogares (ENGHo) 2017-2018, incorporando una distribución diferente de los gastos familiares, especialmente con un mayor peso de los servicios.

item.title: Trump propone a Dana White, presidente de la UFC, como portavoz de la Casa Blanca
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, ha ofrecido a Dana White, presidente de la Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC), el cargo de portavoz de la Casa Blanca a través de su cuenta en Truth Social. En su mensaje, Trump elogió a White como un 'luchador y guerrero implacable', destacando su perfil comunicativo agresivo y directo, que encaja con la estrategia de comunicación de Trump. El mandatario sugirió que White incorporara a su equipo a varios luchadores de la UFC, como Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes y Kayla Harrison, para defender a Estados Unidos 'de la izquierda lunática'. Según CNN, White habría rechazado la propuesta. Dana White, de 57 años, es un empresario estadounidense que ha presidido la UFC desde 2001, cuando la compró junto a los hermanos Fertitta, transformándola de una organización al borde de la quiebra en un negocio multimillonario. White ha mantenido una estrecha relación con Trump desde hace más de dos déca

item.title: El Vaticano lanza Athletica Vaticana, una asociación deportiva para promover la fraternidad y la inclusión
item.description: El Vaticano ha creado una asociación deportiva llamada Athletica Vaticana, que busca promover valores como la fraternidad, la paz y la inclusión a través del deporte. La iniciativa comenzó en 2017 cuando un grupo de trabajadores del Vaticano que se reunían para correr decidió organizarse como una comunidad deportiva. En 2018, la Santa Sede y el Comité Olímpico Nacional Italiano firmaron un acuerdo para permitir que Athletica Vaticana compitiera fuera de la Ciudad del Vaticano. La asociación, fundada oficialmente el 1 de enero de 2019, está formada por más de 500 miembros, incluyendo guardias suizos, monjas, sacerdotes, trabajadores de museos y personal de mantenimiento. Además de atletismo, la asociación ha incorporado otros deportes como ciclismo, pádel, tenis, taekwondo, cricket, esgrima, remo, baloncesto y natación. El objetivo no es ganar medallas, sino usar el deporte como herramienta para acercar mensajes de fraternidad, paz, solidaridad e inclusión. El Papa Francisco ha respalda

item.title: La Junta de Castilla y León limita financiación a obras con 'adoctrinamiento', generando debate sobre censura en cultura y educación
item.description: La nueva cláusula de la Junta de Castilla y León que restringe la financiación pública a producciones que impliquen 'adoctrinamiento ideológico, propaganda partidista o apoyo expreso a opciones políticas concretas' ha generado un intenso debate sobre las prácticas de censura promovidas por Vox en ámbitos culturales y educativos. El productor de cine Olmo Dalcó, quien utiliza un pseudónimo para proteger su identidad, denuncia que su proyecto sobre la represión durante la dictadura franquista podría quedar sin financiación por esta normativa. La Consejería de Cultura, en manos de Vox, niega que se trate de censura y asegura que la evaluación correrá a cargo de 'una comisión de expertos', aunque no ha especificado los criterios para determinar qué proyectos recibirán apoyo. En el ámbito educativo, Vox ha impulsado medidas como el pin parental para limitar la participación de menores en talleres de educación sexual, y en 2025 presentó una Proposición No de Ley para retirar libros considera

item.title: China logra un avance en la eficiencia de IA al generar más tokens de inferencia que los consumidos en su entrenamiento
item.description: La noticia aborda un hito tecnológico logrado por China en el campo de la inteligencia artificial, destacando que por primera vez los modelos de IA generan más tokens de inferencia que los que consumen durante su entrenamiento. Los tokens son la unidad mínima con la que los modelos procesan texto, funcionando como una moneda digital en el funcionamiento de la IA. Este avance es significativo porque, aunque el uso de IA puede parecer gratuito tras pagar una suscripción, el consumo de tokens representa un coste operativo variable y difícil de predecir para las empresas. El informe respaldado por el gobierno chino señala que la cantidad de datos de inferencia generados supera a los datos utilizados en el entrenamiento, lo que representa un cambio fundamental en la economía de tokens. Este logro se enmarca en la estrategia china de mejorar la 'economía de tokens' mediante 'fábricas de tokens' y plataformas de distribución, enfocándose en optimizar el consumo energético y operativo. item.title: La democracia de las abejas: cómo un enjambre elige su hogar sin un líder
item.description:
El documental «Las abejas votan mejor que tu junta de vecinos 🐝» explora una de las formas más sorprendentes de toma de decisiones colectivas en la naturaleza: la elección de una nueva vivienda por parte de un enjambre de abejas. A través de los experimentos del biólogo Thomas Seeley, de la Universidad Cornell, explica cómo miles de individuos pueden alcanzar una decisión eficaz sin un líder que imponga su criterio. El relato también conecta este comportamiento con el funcionamiento de los grupos humanos y los mecanismos de decisión del cerebro.

Un enjambre que busca casa sin una reina que decida

Cuando un enjambre abandona su colmena, miles de abejas obreras se agrupan alrededor de su reina. Su objetivo es encontrar un nuevo refugio donde establecerse y pasar el invierno. Aunque la reina forma parte esencial de la colonia, no es ella quien decide dónde vivir. La elección recae en un grupo de exploradoras que buscan posibles emplazamientos y

item.title: Renault advierte de que la producción automovilística europea podría reducirse a la mitad tras 2030 por la competencia china
item.description: Renault ha alertado sobre una posible reducción drástica de la producción automovilística en Europa debido a la creciente competencia de los fabricantes chinos. El director general de la compañía, François Provost, ha expuesto en un encuentro con periodistas en Londres que, si la Unión Europea no adopta medidas, la producción de coches en el continente podría caer a la mitad de su media histórica antes de 2030. Según Provost, los fabricantes chinos pueden importar sus vehículos a Europa con costes entre un 30% y un 40% inferiores a los de sus competidores europeos, una diferencia que Renault no puede compensar en las condiciones actuales. La propuesta de Provost consiste en exigir a las marcas chinas que fabriquen en Europa si desean vender en el mercado europeo, vinculando el acceso al mercado con la producción local. Esta medida busca asegurar que el crecimiento de las marcas chinas también genere empleo y actividad industrial en el continente. Sin embargo, la propuesta no resuelve a

item.title: Relato ganador de concurso de terror 'Carpaccio' explora temas de maternidad y supervivencia
item.description: La revista Nexiok ha anunciado el relato 'Carpaccio', de Violeta Sánchez Pintado, como ganador de su primera convocatoria de relatos de terror. El relato, valorado con un 9,5 sobre 10 por los editores Charlie Marrez y Tom Soren, combina elementos de amor, maternidad, ternura y horror corporal en una narrativa que logra mantener una coherencia emocional y narrativa a lo largo de menos de mil palabras. La historia sigue a una madre que, tras un incidente traumático en el que su marido intenta asesinar a su hija, huye con la niña hacia una cabaña en el bosque. En un contexto postapocalíptico donde los recursos son escasos y los supermercados están vacíos, la protagonista enfrenta la difícil decisión de alimentar a su hija con carne humana, específicamente de su propio antebrazo, para evitar que muera de hambre. La narrativa explora temas profundos como la supervivencia extrema, la relación madre-hija y la moralidad en situaciones límite, manteniendo un tono natural y cotidiano que contras

item.title: Ataque con drones en Bolívar deja tres militares muertos y ocho heridos
item.description: Un ataque con drones explosivos en el sur del departamento de Bolívar, en el noroeste de Colombia, ha dejado tres militares muertos y ocho heridos, según informaron las autoridades castrenses. El incidente, ocurrido este sábado, ha provocado una intensa movilización de efectivos militares en la zona, con el objetivo de evaluar el impacto del ataque y identificar a los responsables. El presidente colombiano, Abelardo de la Espriella, ha condenado el ataque en sus redes sociales, advirtiendo que 'no se dejarán intimidar ni retroceder' frente a la escalada de ataques contra las Fuerzas Armadas. El mandatario ha asegurado que 'no tendrán escondite ni tregua' los responsables del atentado, prometiendo perseguirlos 'con toda la fuerza legítima del Estado' hasta desmantelar sus organizaciones criminales. Además, el presidente ha reafirmado su compromiso con la defensa del territorio colombiano, señalando que 'en la patria milagro, el terrorismo no tiene cabida y la autoridad se respeta'. Segú

item.title: 5.000 personas exigen una moratoria a los centros de datos en Aragón por su impacto en agua, energía y territorio
item.description: Una manifestación de aproximadamente 5.000 personas en Zaragoza, convocada por la campaña internacional 'Stop Dirty Data Centres', ha exigido una moratoria a la expansión de los centros de datos en Aragón. La movilización, que se desarrolló este sábado en el marco de las jornadas de acción de la campaña, denunció el impacto de estas infraestructuras en el agua, la energía y el territorio, y reclamó frenar un modelo que convierte Aragón en una 'granja energética' al servicio de las grandes tecnológicas. Los participantes destacaron que los centros de datos consumen recursos de manera desproporcionada, generan efectos como islas de calor y ruido, y no aportan empleo significativo, a pesar de las promesas de las empresas. Isabel, activista de 'No es sequía, es saqueo', explicó que los centros de datos no llegan a generar 200 empleos frente a los más de mil anunciados, y cuestionó la opacidad que rodea estos proyectos. El manifiesto leído al final de la marcha frente al Edificio Pignatelli

item.title: El error científico y el error racial de Theophilus Painter
item.description: La noticia relata dos errores históricos cometidos por Theophilus Painter, un científico y posteriormente presidente de la Universidad de Texas. En 1921, Painter, como zoólogo, contó 24 cromosomas en las células sexuales humanas, una cifra que se mantuvo aceptada durante más de 30 años. Sin embargo, en 1955, el citogenetista Joe Hin Tjio descubrió que los humanos tienen 23 cromosomas, lo que llevó a la comprensión de que el cromosoma 2 humano se formó por la fusión de dos cromosomas ancestrales. Este hallazgo confirmó la evolución humana y la relación con los simios. Por otro lado, en 1946, Painter, como presidente universitario, negó la admisión de Heman Marion Sweatt, un afroamericano, basándose en su raza. Esta decisión llevó a una demanda que culminó en una sentencia del Tribunal Supremo en 1950, que favoreció a Sweatt y marcó un hito en la lucha contra la segregación racial en Estados Unidos.
